gloss: forcibly; compulsorily; if pressed; if I must say

definitions.explanation: Doing something against one's will or nature, or making someone do something unwillingly.

definitions.gloss: if pressed; if I must say; dare I say
definitions.explanation: Used when offering an opinion reluctantly or when pressed to give an answer even though one doesn't have a strong opinion.

examples.japanese: {強|し}いて{言|い}えば、{赤|あか}より{青|あお}のほうが{好|す}きかな。
examples.english: If I had to say, I guess I like blue more than red.

examples.japanese: {強|し}いて{参加|さんか}する{必要|ひつよう}はない。
examples.english: You don't need to force yourself to participate.

examples.japanese: {強|し}いて{挙|あ}げるなら、{時間|じかん}が{足|た}りなかったことが{問題|もんだい}だった。
examples.english: If I had to point out something, the problem was that we didn't have enough time.

notes:
TWO MAIN USES:

1) FORCIBLY: Against one's will
・{強|し}いて〜する (to do ~ by force)
・{強|し}いて〜させる (to force someone to ~)

2) IF PRESSED: Reluctant opinion
・{強|し}いて{言|い}えば (if I had to say)
・{強|し}いて{挙|あ}げれば/なら (if I had to pick/mention)
・{強|し}いて{選|えら}ぶなら (if I had to choose)

COMMON PATTERN:
{強|し}いて〜ば/なら is very common for hedging opinions:
・{強|し}いて{言|い}えば、〜かな (If I had to say... maybe ~)

NUANCE:
In sense 2, {強|し}いて signals that the speaker doesn't have a strong preference but is answering because asked. It's a polite way to give a lukewarm opinion without sounding too definitive.

ETYMOLOGY:
From the verb {強|し}いる (to force, to compel) in て-form.
